result: A CRISPR screen using the HuEpi library in conjunction with AZD5582 & I-BET151 identified INTS12 as a top hit to improve this LRA combination. The screen also identified previously validated genes and other candidates predicted to improve the LRA combination in both J-Lat cell lines tested.
evaluation: All reviewers affirm the screening strategy and identification of INTS12. One reviewer states the work is 'based on a sound strategy for screening targets to activate HIV latency,' another notes 'the authors employed a high-throughput CRISPR screening strategy' and found INTS12, and a third emphasizes 'the authors successfully identified, through multiple techniques, INTS12.' No concerns were raised about the screen methodology or hit identification.

result: Knockout of INTS12 reactivates HIV on its own and improves reactivation with AZD5582 & I-BET151 treatment in J-Lat cell lines. INTS12 KO shows the most HIV reactivation when combined with AZD5582 & I-BET151, as measured by virus release assays and flow cytometry. Complementation experiments confirmed INTS12 is responsible for the negative effect on HIV expression.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings without challenge. One reviewer notes 'findings were confirmed through multiple screens and multiple techniques,' and another states the authors 'have included new data and clarifications which help strengthen their conclusions.' The complementation data and cell viability controls are not questioned.

result: RNA-seq analysis showed that INTS12 knockout more specifically reactivates HIV compared to AZD5582 & I-BET151 treatment alone, with only 70 upregulated and 3 downregulated genes. The combination of INTS12 KO with AZD5582 & I-BET151 increases the potency of reactivation (fold change ~28) but with some loss of specificity (255 upregulated, 159 downregulated genes). INTS12 KO is still more specific than PMAi treatment.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the RNA-seq findings or the specificity claims. One reviewer explicitly notes 'the rigor of exploring the mechanism of INTS12 repression of HIV transcriptional elongation' as a strength. The revised manuscript is described as having 'new data and clarifications which help strengthen their conclusions.'

result: INTS12 is present on chromatin at the promoter of HIV as shown by CUT&Tag data, with localization extending past the LTR to sites of pausing. This suggests INTS12 may be acting directly on viral transcription.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm this finding. One states 'the authors successfully mapped the identified HIV silencing factor at the HIV promoter.' The CUT&Tag data and interpretation of direct binding are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: CUT&Tag data for RNAPII (RPB3) and elongation-competent RNAPII (Ser2p) show a dramatic increase in RNAPII occupancy in the gene body of HIV only with the combination of INTS12 KO and AZD5582 & I-BET151, not with either treatment alone. This indicates INTS12 induces a transcriptional elongation block that is overcome by the combination.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this mechanistic finding. One reviewer highlights 'the solid mechanistic insights it provides on INTS12 repression of transcriptional elongation' and another emphasizes 'the rigor of exploring the mechanism of INTS12 repression of HIV transcriptional elongation' as a strength. No concerns are raised about the CUT&Tag data or interpretation.

result: Knockout of INTS12 increased HIV-1 reactivation in CD4 T cells from virally suppressed PLWH ex vivo. INTS12 KO alone showed statistically significant increases in viral RNA in four out of six donors, and the combination with AZD5582 & I-BET151 showed further increases in four out of six donors. Viral RNA was detected in the supernatant from all three donors tested for this measurement, indicating full-length HIV RNA production.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm these primary cell findings. One notes 'the effect of its knock down in inducing HIV transcription in primary cells, albeit in only a subset of donors, is intriguing.' Another states 'findings were confirmed through multiple screens and multiple techniques.' The caveat about subset responsiveness is acknowledged but does not undermine support for the finding.

result: A second CRISPR screen targeting all Integrator complex members predicted that the cleavage module, phosphatase module, and core (in addition to INTS12) are all involved in HIV-1 latency control and can be targeted to improve AZD5582 & I-BET151 treatment. The SOSS complex and enhancer/arm module did not score positively.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this screen or its predictions. One reviewer notes the work provides 'solid mechanistic insights' and another emphasizes the 'rigor' of the mechanistic exploration. The Screen #2 data and predictions are accepted without critique.

result: INTS12 knockout increases reactivation with diverse classes of LRAs including TNF-α, anti-CD3/CD28, and SAHA, suggesting INTS12 is a general block to HIV reactivation.
evaluation: While reviewers do not explicitly challenge this finding, one reviewer notes as a 'minor point' that 'there was an opportunity to examine a larger panel of latency reversal agents that reactivate by different mechanisms to determine whether INTS12 and transcriptional elongation are limiting for a broad spectrum of latency reversal agents.' This suggests the evidence for generality is accepted but could be strengthened.

result: Tazemetostat (EZH2 inhibitor) increases reactivation of HIV-1 in the presence of AZD5582 & I-BET151 to much higher levels than either treatment alone, validating a screen prediction.
evaluation: This validation of a screen hit is not questioned by reviewers. It serves as supporting evidence for the screening approach's validity.

result: INTS12 knockdown does not grossly affect cell viability according to previous studies, and the authors propose targeting INTS12 with a small-molecule drug may be successful in the shock-and-kill approach, though the function of INTS12 in diverse T cell functions or in vivo is not yet known.
evaluation: One reviewer explicitly notes as a 'weakness' that 'the impact of INTS12 in diverse T cell functions or other in vivo functions is not yet known, but the authors acknowledge this in the revised discussion.' This indicates the proposal is speculative and the caveat is appropriately acknowledged.

result: This study is the first to report analysis of an Integrator complex member in ex vivo experiments with cells from virally suppressed PLWH, demonstrating that CRISPR-screening in cell line models can identify blocks to reactivation relevant to primary cells.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the novelty and significance. One states 'the finding that INTS12 may play a role in HIV latency is novel,' and another notes the work 'successfully identified, through multiple techniques, INTS12' and that 'knockdown of INTS12 does not induce toxic effects in the cells, thus rendering it a candidate a drug discovery campaign.'

result: Small-molecule drugs targeting INTS12 or Integrator complex members are not yet available, but their development would be predicted to improve the efficacy of existing LRAs for viral reactivation and reservoir reduction.
evaluation: Reviewers support this as a future direction. One states 'future studies are needed to explore INTS12 as a drug target against HIV/AIDS,' and another notes INTS12 is 'a candidate a drug discovery campaign aimed at finding new agents for an HIV/AIDS cure.'
